Let R be an excellent local ring, reduce nilpotents, and fix a proper primary ideal a. A zero-dimensional reduction has empty centred boundary and its unique empty envelope. In positive dimension set X=V_a(R), retaining EVERY prime support strictly below the maximal ideal. The sole imported premise is the ENTIRE qualified G331: the independently geometric core consists of actual negative effective finite real Cartier presentations on directed ACTUAL primary blowups, with nonnegative degree on every contracted proper integral curve; its uniform class C and actual decreasing-net class D agree with the ideal classes. Its rational density, finite maxima, full-fibre positive descent and precisely scoped smooth comparison are used with all qualifications. No envelope is granted.

For any finite continuous signed obstacle f define A_0=R and A_m={g in R: v(g)+m f(v)>=0 for EVERY v in X}, h_m=-v(A_m)/m. With c=max(0,-min f), a^N is contained in A_m whenever N>0 and N>=mc. Ultrametric addition and nonnegative ring values make A_m an ideal. If f is negative somewhere, no unit belongs, so EVERY positive-degree A_m is proper primary; otherwise A_m=R. Thus h_m is finite continuous, lies below f, and has actual geometric positivity on Bl_(A_m)(R). Multiplication gives A_m A_n contained in A_(m+n). A monic ideal-integrality equation proves A_m integrally closed: a finite v(g)<v(A_m) would make its leading term uniquely least. Infinite g values are automatic; primary ideal values are finite.

The raw function p(f)=sup{u in D:u<=f} equals both the supremum over C competitors and sup_m h_m. A rational competitor -v(I)/r<=f has I contained in A_r. Approximate a C competitor uniformly by rational profiles and shift down by an arbitrarily small rational a-constant, realized by ideal multiplication after clearing denominators. For u=inf_i g_i<=f in an ACTUAL decreasing C-net, the directed open sets {g_i<f+epsilon} cover compact X. One index works everywhere, so g_i-epsilon is a C competitor and u<=sup_m h_m+epsilon. Let epsilon decrease to zero. This includes bottom and partial poles and uses continuity of f, not of u.

Put M_1=||v(A_1)|| and H_N=max_(r<=N) h_r. Writing m=kr+s, 0<=s<r, grading gives h_m>=(kr/m)h_r-sM_1/m>=h_r-rM_1/m. Hence H_N-NM_1/m<=h_m<=p(f). The FULL sequence converges pointwise to the finite nonpositive lower-semicontinuous p(f). Continuity of p(f) is equivalent to uniform H_N convergence and to uniform full h_m convergence: compact increasing strict-error open covers prove the forward implication, the residue estimate transfers it to h_m, and uniform closedness of C proves the converse. General positivity or USC regularization is NOT inferred. Raw envelopes are sup-norm 1-Lipschitz: if f<=g+epsilon then any D minorant u of f has u-epsilon in D below g. Therefore uniform approximation by obstacles with actual C envelopes gives a C envelope for the limit, without asserting such density generally.

The fixed canonical algebra A=direct-sum A_m t^m is finitely generated iff p(f) is a rational unit-or-primary profile, iff p(f) is a finite maximum of canonical profiles. For finite homogeneous generators g_i t^(d_i), choose L divisible by all d_i, D_0=max d_i, and J=(g_i^(L/d_i)). At every support some generator has finite value, since A_1 is primary or unit. Degree-m expressions have value at least m min_i v(g_i)/d_i. Pure powers in A_L show p(f)=h_L=-v(J)/L=max_(r<=D_0)h_r. The generator coefficient ideal contains A_1 in its radical, making J primary in the proper case. Consequently 0<=p(f)-h_m<=D_0 M_1/m uniformly on ALL supports.

Conversely if p(f)=-v(J)/q with J proper primary, the definition and h_m<=p(f)<=f give A_m={g:v(g)>=(m/q)v(J) on all X}={g:g^q in integral-closure(J^m)}. The latter equality uses the centred rank-one DVR criterion on EVERY minimal-component quotient, followed by the all-minimal-component criterion SH6.8.3--4/1.1.5. Every component has positive dimension: a zero-dimensional minimal component would make the maximal ideal minimal and the local reduction zero-dimensional. Monic equations give the reverse inequalities on every nonminimal support. Let B=R[Jt^q]. A primary ideal contains a regular element by prime avoidance; B is reduced excellent with total quotient product K_j(t^q). The extension product K_j(t) is finite, possibly inseparable. Excellent/Nagata finite normalization gives a finite B-module. For g in A_m, the equation for g^q over J^m makes g^q t^(mq) integral over B and then gt^m integral by its qth-power equation. A contains B and is a B-submodule of that finite normalization, hence finite. The unit case is R[t]; a finite maximum is rational by sums of powered ideals. No general finite generation is presumed.

For a signed integral exceptional Cartier obstacle f_D on an actual primary blowup over normal R, its normalized model Y gives exactly A_m=H^0(Y,O(mD)) intersect R in the canonical rational trivialization. Boundary tests at exceptional height-one orders and regularity elsewhere imply the section containment by normal height-one intersection. Conversely pull a section to the valuation ring of Frac(R/p) for EACH support p. Its invertible lattice has a nonzero generic trivialization outside the exceptional fibre, and the coefficient inequality is v(g)+m f_D(v)>=0. Properness gives the valued centre. No original fraction field is mapped through p. Finite generation of this particular section-intersection algebra remains a hypothesis.

For another primary b let d(v)=v(b)>0 and T(v)=v/d(v), with f_b(Tv)=f_a(v)/d(v). The canonical inequalities divide by d; ALL A_m and their algebra are literally unchanged. Profiles and envelopes divide by d, with exact three-gauge cocycle and uniform constants divided by min d. Finite normalization S gives A_m^R=A_m^S intersect R. Source envelopes descend positively only when constant on EVERY fibre, including the conductor-infinite quotient stratum; then comparison with all pulled-back competitors proves the downstairs envelope. Obstacle compatibility alone is insufficient. A decreasing family with envelopes H_i in C has the ACTUAL D envelope inf H_i of the infimum obstacle, including poles and bottom.

On excellent reduced curves every normalization centre is a DVR and a regular conductor element has finite branch order, so all boundary fibres are singleton. Actual geometric real Cartier slopes on each DVR, semilocal gluing and positive descent give the full finite nonpositive orthant; decreasing truncations give the extended orthant. Thus the geometric envelope is min(f,0), matching the ideal envelope. The literal classical/CLD multibranch radial class remains distinct. On a DVR an irrational obstacle -alpha has continuous real Cartier envelope and A_m=(x^ceil(m alpha)); finite homogeneous generators would force a rational minimum order/degree slope, contradicting alpha. Non-finite-generation therefore proves no CE failure.

notes.text:
Scope: S is the local ring of a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, dimension at least two. DVR and empty cases are direct in n1. The supports, completion homeomorphism and primary contraction are those of the ENTIRE qualified G331. Its full smooth comparison identifies C with the finite continuous BFJ class and D with the full all-retraction BFJ class, bottom adjoined. It grants no envelope theorem.

A NEW published application uses BFJ, Valuations and plurisubharmonic singularities, Definitions3.15--3.17, Proposition3.18 and its ENTIRE immediate proof including Lemma3.22, and its function version Remark3.21. Exact setting, retractions, PA density, closed-simplex continuity, multiplier units and complete auxiliary proofs through3.25 were physically read in bounded untruncated windows. Smooth Hironaka principalization, multiplier subadditivity [DEL]/Lazarsfeld9.5, thinness computations and smooth Izumi are disclosed deeper foundations; their historical proofs are not freshly recursively audited. First use the maximal-ideal gauge and let F be continuous and determined on one dual complex, F=F composed with r_pi0. Signed real primary ideal profiles have this property on a common principalization (BFJ1.14); they are uniformly dense (1.15). Put M=max(0,-min F). The constant -M is a nef barrier. The coefficientwise supremum W of nef Weil divisors below Z(F) is finite nef: replace competitors by their maxima with -M, making them directed with bounded coefficients, and take their weak limit in the closed nef cone. Thus -M<=W<=0 and W<=Z(F).

Let H be the formal psh function of W (BFJ3.11), with H(v)=inf_pi H(r_pi v) on EVERY semivaluation. On closed simplices the inequality H<=F follows from divisorial density and the actual closed-simplex continuity theorem. For refinements pi>=pi0, F(r_pi v)=F(v); taking the cofinal retraction infimum gives H<=F on every support. Also H>=-M. Every nonbottom u in D below F has finite nef coefficients below W by G331's exact smooth comparison, hence its full extension is below H. Bottom causes no exception. Therefore H is already the greatest D minorant as a raw function; continuity is still to prove.

Set B_m=L-infinity(mW)=L-infinity(mZ(F)) in the completed ring, using BFJ3.17. They contain m-hat^ceil(mM), with a positive power chosen in the unit case. They contract exactly to the canonical A_m of n1. Here is the all-support check, rather than a divisorial-only identification. If g passes the coefficient tests, choose N>0, N>=mM. The primary-or-unit ideal (g)+m-hat^N has divisorial log-profile max(log|g|,-N)<=mF. Its full primary-profile extension satisfies this inequality on closed simplices and then on all supports by the preceding cofinal-retraction argument. Since v(g)>=v((g)+m-hat^N), the canonical inequality follows. The reverse direction is its divisorial restriction. Exact primary contraction and the completion homeomorphism give the local S ideals. All infinite g values are automatic.

If W=0 then F>=0 by divisorial density and continuity, and every envelope/profile is zero. Otherwise BFJ3.14 makes H strictly negative. It is continuous and strictly negative on the fixed compact complex, where thinness A is bounded. The constant C in BFJ3.18 may be chosen finite with A<=-CW THERE; no global thinness bound is used. For positive real t write W_t=Z(L-infinity(tW))/t. The published inequality is W_t<=W<=(1-C/t)W_(t-C) for t>C. At t=m+C it gives (1+C/m)W<=W_m<=W. These inequalities extend through closed simplices and ALL retraction infima to EVERY support. The extension of W_m is h_m=-v(A_m)/m, so

0 <= H-h_m <= CM/m for EVERY m>=1 and every semivaluation.

This proves uniform approximation by actual negative effective primary Cartier profiles, hence H belongs to the continuous independently geometric C. Canonical finite generation was never assumed. It is a fixed-model smooth correction, not a singular Jacobian correction or positivity assigned to USC regularization.

For arbitrary finite continuous signed F choose signed primary model functions F_j converging uniformly. Their actual C envelopes H_j exist by the model estimate. The raw sup-norm Lipschitz estimate from n1 makes H_j uniformly Cauchy and identifies the limit with p(F). Uniform closedness of C proves the greatest continuous geometric envelope for EVERY such F. notes.text:
Complete scoped theorem: let S be a positive-dimensional smooth affine CLOSED local germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, let a finite group G act faithfully by local automorphisms, and assume R=S^G is excellent Noetherian with S finite over R. Then EVERY finite continuous signed obstacle on V_a(R), for EVERY proper primary gauge a, has a greatest continuous independently geometric C/D envelope. This includes actual normal nonisolated quotient singularities. It is not a theorem for arbitrary excellent normal germs.

R is normal: an element of Frac(R) integral over R is integral over normal S, hence belongs to S, and its invariance puts it in R. Let b=aS and rho:V_b(S)->V_a(R). The ENTIRE qualified G331 gives continuous surjective restriction and positive class pullback, retaining ALL supports. Set K=Frac(R), L=Frac(S). An invariant fraction has denominator cleared by the product of its G-translates, showing L^G=K. Here is the fixed-field proof needed, without an extra grant. Distinct automorphisms are L-linearly independent as functions: subtracting sigma_j(a) times a minimal relation at x from its relation at ax gives a shorter nonzero relation when two automorphisms differ on a. Evaluation columns therefore span L^d, d=|G|; otherwise an annihilating row gives a relation. Choose x_1,...,x_d with invertible evaluation matrix. For x in L solve sigma_i(x)=sum c_j sigma_i(x_j). Applying any group element permutes rows, so uniqueness makes each c_j invariant, hence in K. The x_j are K-linearly independent by the same matrix, so [L:K]=d. The polynomial over the distinct orbit of any x is separable with invariant coefficients, and its minimal polynomial divides it and splits in L. Thus L/K is Galois with group G. Normal S is the integral closure of R in L.

The decisive ALL-FIBRE step uses the full qualified G331 coefficient-norm trace and its proved full fibre support. Taking splitting field L and a lift w on its finite integral closure S, that grant gives

mu_v = sum_(sigma in G) delta_(w composed with sigma), with support(mu_v)=rho^(-1)(v).

Therefore every restriction fibre is exactly the full G-orbit of any of its points. Repeated orbit points carry multiplicity in the measure. The grant proves its coefficient identity in valued QUOTIENT fraction fields after killing supports; we do not extend a nonzero-support semivaluation to the original field L. No nonminimal or singular-supported point is lost.

For downstairs f set F=f composed with rho. By n2 its source envelope H_S belongs to C_S. Each group element preserves F and both geometric classes, so uniqueness of the greatest minorant makes H_S invariant. Full orbit fibres make it fibre constant. G331's positive continuous descent supplies a unique H_R in C_R with rho^*H_R=H_S. Surjectivity gives H_R<=f. Any u in D_R below f pulls back to a source D minorant below H_S, hence u<=H_R. Thus P_R(f)=H_R and rho^*P_R(f)=P_S(f composed with rho). This proves actual positivity and continuity, rather than positivity of a raw supremum or USC regularization. No finite-generation or contact-sector hypothesis is used.

There is explicit actual primary Cartier approximation downstairs. Let B_m=A_m^S(F), which is G-stable by its defining all-support inequalities. Choose finite R-module generators s_i of B_m and form the coefficient norm polynomial

N_(L(T)/K(T))(sum T_i s_i)=product_(sigma in G)(sum T_i sigma(s_i)).

Let J_m be its coefficient ideal in R. Coefficients lie in K and are integral over normal R, hence in R. G331 proves independence of generators, primary-power containment and the ALL-support identity v(J_m)=sum_sigma (w composed with sigma)(B_m)=d w(B_m). Consequently kappa_m=-v(J_m)/(dm) pulls back to h_m^S=-w(B_m)/m. The ideal is proper primary in the nonzero case and unit in the zero case. Each kappa_m is an actual negative effective nef Cartier profile on Bl_(J_m)(R), below f, and they converge uniformly to P_R(f), by n2 and n1's smooth uniform criterion. Surjective restriction preserves the sup norm. There is no finite-flat determinant-norm assumption. Also A_m^R(f)=B_m intersect R exactly; no finite generation is inferred by contraction.

For EVERY signed REAL exceptional Cartier model obstacle on an actual primary blowup over R, G331's exact evaluation formula writes it as a finite signed real primary-ideal combination with a fixed primary section correction. Pullback to S is determined on one BFJ complex after smooth common principalization. In n2's maximal-ideal gauge let M,C be its model constants and let e=CM/min_(nu in V_mS(S)) nu(b). The denominator is positive by primaryness. Gauge transport and the norm identity give 0<=P_R(f)-kappa_m<=e/m uniformly on ALL supports. Hence J_m is contained in A_(dm)^R and h_(dm)^R>=kappa_m. For k>=d write m=floor(k/d), r=dm, with k-r<d. Grading with (A_1^R)^(k-r) and nonpositivity imply h_k^R>=h_r^R-d M_1^R/k. Therefore for k>=2d,

0 <= P_R(f)-h_k^R <= e/floor(k/d)+d M_1^R/k <= (2de+d M_1^R)/k.

This is a full-degree fixed-obstacle uniform estimate WITHOUT canonical finite generation. All ideals are primary or unit in every degree. The constants depend on the obstacle and smooth model. No general singular thinness estimate, universal primary correction, or conclusion about arbitrary excellent germs follows.

Actual example: for r>=1 take S=k[x,y,z_1,...,z_r] localized at the origin, with the involution (x,y,z)->(-x,-y,z). Invariant monomials are generated by a=x^2,b=xy,c=y^2,z_i; the only relation is ac=b^2, checked by reduced monomial images. Thus R=k[a,b,c,z_1,...,z_r]/(ac-b^2) localized at the origin. The extension is finite via the quadratic equations for x,y; orbit products of denominators verify the local invariant equality, and the origin is the unique point above the origin. R is excellent normal of dimension r+2. Its singular locus (a,b,c) has dimension r: away from it a derivative is a unit, while there the local quadratic relation has no linear term and embedding dimension exceeds dimension by one. This is a normal NONISOLATED domain.

For r=1 let m=(a,b,c,z), I=(a+b,b+c,z)+m^2 and J=(a,c,z^2)+m^3, and take f(v)=v(I)-5/4+sin(v(J))/100. Both ideals are primary, so this is a finite continuous signed obstacle on EVERY support. On the cover substitute x=r_0, y=r_0(h-1), keeping z, and use monomial weights (1,1,6) on (r_0,h,z). The substitution is injective. Restriction gives m value two; a+b=x(x+y) and b+c=y(x+y) have weight three, so normalized v(I)=3/2 and v(J)=1. The monomial valuation of (x,y,z) with weights (1,1,6) has identical a,b,c,z values but v(I)=1 and v(J)=1. The obstacle is respectively 1/4+sin(1)/100>0 and -1/4+sin(1)/100<0. It detects cancellation despite identical coordinate weights. Its continuous geometric envelope is constructed by the norm primary profiles; no closed formula or finite-generation assertion for this particular nonlinear example is claimed.

All primary gauges obey n1's exact cocycle and unchanged canonical ideals. R is already normal, so this cover is NOT its birational normalization; fibre orbit compatibility is proved. For arbitrary nonnormal germs only the conditional full-conductor rule in n1 is obtained.
